property_summary: For every 4-byte interfaceId input, the reference contract returns true exactly when the id equals IERC165's interfaceId (type(IERC165).interfaceId) and false otherwise; the mutant inverts this for that specific id so the property (supportsInterface(id) == (id == type(IERC165).interfaceId)) holds for all inputs on the reference but is violated by the mutant for the IERC165 id.
For any 4-byte interfaceId, the reference returns true iff the id equals IERC165's interfaceId; the mutant flips the result for that specific id causing a mismatch for that input.

For every 4-byte interfaceId, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true exactly when the id equals IERC165's interfaceId; the mutant flips that comparison so it returns false for IERC165's id (violating the rule for that input).

For every 4-byte interfaceId input, the reference contract's supportsInterface returns true exactly when the id equals IERC165's interfaceId; the mutant negates that comparison and thus returns false for IERC165's id, violating the rule for that specific input.

For every 4-byte interfaceId input, the reference contract reports support for IERC165 exactly when interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId (i.e. supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) == true), while the mutant flips that specific result and will return false for IERC165's interface id.

For any interfaceId, the reference contract reports support for IERC165 (true when queried with IERC165 interface id) by deferring to super.supportsInterface, whereas the mutant incorrectly returns false for IERC165.interfaceId (breaking that rule for those inputs).

For every bytes4 interfaceId, the reference contract C reports support for IERC165.interfaceId when queried (because it defers to super.supportsInterface), whereas the mutant returns false for IERC165.interfaceId — so the property is: C.supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) always returns true; the mutant returns false for that input.

For every bytes4 iface id, the reference C reports support for IAccessControl.interfaceId OR IERC165.interfaceId (i.e., C.supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) is true), whereas the mutant that stops deferring to super fails to report support for IERC165.interfaceId — so the property: calling supportsInterface with the IERC165 interface id never reverts and returns true on the reference, but the mutant returns false for that input.

For every bytes4 iface id, C.supportsInterface(iface) returns true when iface == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or iface == type(IERC165).interfaceId (because C defers to super which reports IERC165), but the mutant that stops deferring will return false for IERC165.interfaceId, so the property is that supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) returns true on the reference and the mutant returns false for that input.

For every bytes4 id, the reference C reports support for the IERC165 interface id (supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) returns true and does not revert), whereas the mutant that stops deferring to super will return false for that interface id; the test fuzzes an arbitrary bytes4 but specifically asserts that calling supportsInterface(type(IERC165).interfaceId) completes and returns true (a rule the mutant breaks for that input).

For every 4-byte interfaceId the reference contract returns true iff the id equals IERC165 or IAccessControl (as implemented by AccessControl.supportsInterface which checks for IAccessControl or IERC165 via super), but the mutant that unconditionally returns true will report support for all ids (violating this distinction) — in particular there exist ids for which reference returns false but mutant returns true.
